name: box-alignment
title: Box alignment
summary: Nine labelled tiles in one 300×300 box, each placed at one of the nine alignments from top-start to bottom-end.
prompt: Place nine labelled tiles in one box, one at each corner, edge midpoint and the centre.
teaches: Overlap children by putting them in a box; each child is laid out on top of the previous one
Place a child at a corner, edge or centre with the box's horizontalAlignment (start/center/end) and verticalAlignment (top/center/bottom)
Give each child its own position by wrapping it in a fillMaxSize box with its own alignment
Make a fixed-width label tile from a single text: width, clip, background, vertical padding and textAlign center

snippets.note: top-start: a fillMaxSize box with horizontalAlignment start, verticalAlignment top
the outer box stacks nine full-size layers
a tile as one text: fillMaxWidth 0.3 (never overlaps when narrow), clip, background, padding [0, 11], textAlign center

check.describe: Tiles at the four corners, the four edge midpoints and the centre of the padded box. Resized (200×300, 450×220) the tiles stay at the nine anchors: each tile is 30 % of the width, so they never overlap, and labels that no longer fit end in an ellipsis.

pitfalls: Alignment belongs to the container, not the child: there is no per-child align modifier, and contentAlignment is not a JSON key. Wrap each child in its own fillMaxSize box to align children differently
A box with no children defaults to center/center but one with children defaults to start/top in the Java parser
textAlign centres text only inside the text's own width: give the text a width (or fillMaxWidth), otherwise it wraps its content and there is nothing to centre in
Fixed-width tiles in a box overlap once the box is narrower than three of them: size them as a fraction of the width ({"fillMaxWidth": 0.3}) and give the labels maxLines 1 with an ellipsis
